reason: The text explicitly portrays the Hebrews as a nation and organized people through multiple elements: (1) Direct use of 'ישׂראל' (Israel) as a national designation, particularly in the phrase 'seventy of the elders of Israel' (שִׁבְעִ֖ים מִזִּקְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל), which establishes national governance structures; (2) Repeated references to 'הָעָם' (the people) as a collective entity with boundaries set around them ('הִגְבַּלְתָּ֤ אֶת־ הָעָם֙ סָבִ֣יב'); (3) Institutional structures including priests ('הַכֹּהֲנִים') as a distinct order within the nation; (4) Collective laws and instructions given to the people as a whole nation. While the text emphasizes their covenant relationship with Yahweh, it clearly establishes them as a nation-state with territorial, structural, and political dimensions beyond merely a family lineage or religious followers.
